title: sweet: support replacement panels that need both DSC slices in one packet
head: 05e02f562ce93c0417f1e0c7ce1d4ab33cb8f2b2
body:
Replacement LCD modules sold for the Redmi Note 10 Pro emulate the AMS667YR01 command set through a DSI bridge. ABL still selects `dsi_k6_38_0c_0a_fhd_dsc_video` for them, but on mainline they stay dark with the backlight off.

The difference to downstream is the DSC packetisation: downstream uses `qcom,mdss-dsc-slice-per-pkt = <2>`, i.e. one DSI packet per 1080px line, while mainline msm DSI always sends one packet per 540px slice. The genuine Samsung panel accepts both; these bridges only accept one packet per line.

- **drm/msm/dsi: support multiple DSC slices per packet**: adds a `dsc_slice_per_pkt` field to `struct mipi_dsi_device` and derives the packet word count and packets per line from it (video and command mode). 0 keeps the current behaviour.
- **drm/panel: ams667yr01: send two DSC slices per packet**: sets it to 2 to match downstream.

Tested on sweet with a replacement panel (same two patches on the `v7.1_rc3` tag): image, backlight (0–2047) and touch work. Before, the screen stayed dark. I can't test a genuine panel, but downstream drives it this way too.

Note: mainline 7.3 has an equivalent flag (ffa88de8dd "drm/mipi-dsi: add flag for sending all DSC slices in one packet", `MIPI_DSI_MODE_DSC_ALL_SLICES_IN_PKT`, honoured by msm DSI). On a 7.3-based tree this becomes a one-line change in the panel driver, so the msm DSI commit here can be dropped when the tree moves on.

title: Input: goodix_gtx8 - follow the panel it is integrated with
head: 4fda8008f5aeba7525a7751a67bd447da5cfaf84
body:
On sweet the GT9896 is integrated with the panel and loses power with it. While the panel is blanked, its level-triggered interrupt keeps firing (about 1800 interrupts during a 5 s blank here) and the threaded handler keeps reading the controller.

This makes `goodix_gtx8` a DRM panel follower when the touchscreen node has a `panel` phandle (added to the sweet DT):

- before the panel is disabled or unprepared: interrupt off, controller powered off
- after the panel is enabled: controller powered on, interrupt back on
- after probe the controller stays off until the panel is enabled, so it is only ever powered while the panel is
- panel followers leave system suspend/resume to the panel

Tested on sweet (7.3-based tree): 0 touch interrupts while blanked (was ~1800 per 5 s), touch works right after unblanking, and the touch supplies stay balanced over repeated blank/unblank cycles. Compile-tested on `v7.2`; the follower hooks it uses (`panel_enabled`/`panel_disabling`) already exist there.

Since this driver is still under review upstream, I'm happy to send this to Jens for the next revision of the series as well.

title: drm/panel: ams667yr01: change refresh rate via the vertical front porch
head: d03f8b398dc05bc0caec1e63f96c3628691a90ef
body:
The 90 Hz and 60 Hz modes keep the 120 Hz porches and scale the pixel clock. The downstream driver never does that: it keeps the clock and stretches the vertical front porch (`dfps_immediate_porch_mode_vfp`, `dsi-supported-dfps-list = <120 60>`).

This switches the driver to the same scheme: every mode uses the 120 Hz pixel clock (393.4 MHz), 60 Hz doubles vtotal (vfp 20 → 2452, vtotal 4864), 90 Hz is dropped, and only 120 Hz is marked preferred. Before, `drm_connector_helper_get_modes_fixed()` marked all three as preferred, so userspace could pick any of them.

Tested on sweet with a replacement LCD panel: with the clock-scaled mode (on a 7.1-based tree), switching to 60 Hz with `modetest` garbles the picture and the DSI host reports errors; with this change (on a 7.3-based tree) `modetest` at 60 Hz shows a clean picture. Compile-tested on `v7.2`. I don't have a genuine AMS667YR01 to test, but the timings match downstream.

Known issue, so nobody is surprised: on my tree, switching modes at runtime (120 → 60 → 120 Hz with `modetest`) is not reliable yet. Afterwards vblank waits time out and the system gets slow, and once the RPMh link stalled. I haven't been able to tell whether that comes from the mode timings, the msm modeset path or the replacement panel's bridge. Booting and running at the preferred 120 Hz mode is not affected, and 60 Hz itself displays fine.

title: arm64: dts: qcom: sm7150: Fix QUP wrapper 1 interconnect provider
head: 704b5511f87442f39ed04e9469bdba2fbeed7a89
body:
All QUP wrapper 1 nodes (i2c6-11, spi6-11, uart8/10/11) reference
`&aggre1_noc MASTER_QUP_1`. In qcom,sm7150-rpmh.h the indices are per
provider: MASTER_QUP_1 (2) is a node of aggre2_noc (qhm_qup_north), while
index 2 on aggre1_noc is qhm_tsif. As a result wrapper 1 never votes the
QUP0 BCM (bcm_qup0 = qhm_qup_center + qhm_qup_north).

Effect on xiaomi-sweet: the only remaining QUP0 voter is the Bluetooth
UART (uart3, wrapper 0). Turning Bluetooth off with the screen on causes
`geni_i2c a84000.i2c: Timeout abort_m_cmd` / goodix -110 on the touch
controller and then a hard SoC reset.

Evidence (/sys/kernel/debug/interconnect/interconnect_summary):

before:
  qhm_tsif        <- a84000.i2c, a8c000.i2c   (wrapper 1 voting on TSIF)
  qhm_qup_north   <- no consumers
  qhm_qup_center  2 -> 0 when BT is turned off (only voter 88c000.serial)
  then: geni_i2c a84000.i2c: Timeout abort_m_cmd, goodix -110, SoC reset

after:
  qhm_qup_center  <- 888000.i2c, 890000.i2c, 88c000.serial
  qhm_tsif        <- no consumers
  qhm_qup_north   <- a84000.i2c, a8c000.i2c
  5x bluetoothctl power off/on with touch in use: no hang, BT comes back
  every time.

Tested on Xiaomi Redmi Note 10 Pro (sweet), kernel v7.2.

title: Xiaomi Redmi Note 10 Pro (sweet): speakers and microphone
head: f948f7223047ab319b97b67c9b510a35fc3175ac
body:
Audio support for Xiaomi Redmi Note 10 Pro (sweet, SM7150).

Speakers: 2x Awinic AW88263S on PRIMARY_MI2S
- aw88261: add AW88263S variant (bindings, compatible, register
  differences), don't touch reg 0 for AIF_RX
- q6routing: handle S32_LE
- sm8250 machine driver: 32-bit slots / BCLK x2 on PRIMARY_MI2S_RX,
  only for the new "xiaomi,sweet-sndcard" compatible, so
  tucana/toco/davinci (tfa9874, S16) are unchanged
- sweet dts: both amps, widgets and routing

Microphone: WCD9370 over SoundWire, AMIC1 -> ADC1 -> TX macro
- q6afe: HW vote response carries only the client handle, don't
  read status from it
- sm7150-lpass-lpi: fix swr/dmic pin functions
- sm7150.dtsi: rx/tx/va macros and both SoundWire masters (disabled)
- sm7150.config: QRTR_SMD=y (fixes ADSP/QRTR probe race),
  LPASS_VA_MACRO=m
- sweet dts: WCD9370 codec and capture DAI link

ADSP restart resilience:
- wcd937x, lpass va/tx/rx macro, soundwire qcom: don't latch runtime PM
  errors when LPASS clocks disappear during an ADSP crash, so the card
  survives an ADSP restart instead of failing with -EBUSY

Tested on sweet: speakers and mic work (PipeWire, voice in Firefox),
5/5 reboots with card and HiFi profile. UCM config:
sm7150-mainline/alsa-ucm-conf#4

Note: userspace also needs hexagonrpcd sensorspd started after rootpd,
otherwise the ADSP sensor_process watchdog crashes the ADSP at ~52 s.
That goes to pmaports separately.

title: sweet: charging and fuel gauge fixes (SMB5 / QG)
head: 04be397a8796b9b6906057d9998ae16593dce141
body:
Charging and battery reporting for the Redmi Note 10 Pro (sweet, PM6150).

Driver fixes (generic, apply to every SMB5 / PM6150 QG user):
- qcom_smbx: fix float voltage encoding on SMB5 (3.6 V base, 10 mV steps)
- qcom_smbx: don't scale USBIN voltage twice on SMB5
- qcom_smbx: decode SMB5 charger states (inhibit = 0, pause = 6), so
  taper reports Charging and terminate/inhibit report Full
- qcom_qg: pick the battery current LSB from the ADC range subtype
- qcom_qg: report status from the battery current, or from the charger
  when one is linked via power-supplies
- qcom_qg: estimate capacity from the battery OCV table with IR
  compensation, and smooth it (max 1% per 20 s, monotonic per direction)

sweet DT only (sm7150-xiaomi-common.dtsi untouched):
- USB-C port dual-role with 5V/3A sink PDO, so PD charging works
- battery: K6 Sunwoda 5020 mAh OCV table from the downstream profile,
  4.40 V float, 200 mOhm, 2 A input limit for DCP
- link the fuel gauge to the charger

Tested on sweet, 7.1 kernel:
- FV register 0x1070 = 0x50, battery tops out at ~4.41 V
- PD contract 5 V / 2 A, AICL settles at 2 A
- STATUS Charging during taper, Full after termination, capacity climbs
  to 100% without jumps
- no qcom_qg / qcom_smbx errors in dmesg
- checkpatch --strict: 0 errors, 0 warnings

Other sm7150-xiaomi boards probably need the same dual-role connector,
but I only tested sweet.

title: arm64: dts: qcom: sm7150-xiaomi-davinci: working WCD9375 microphone capture
head: 5ad991e40e8aa1e952d7fab58844e9aa4042f192
body:
Brings WCD9375 capture on Xiaomi Mi 9T (davinci) to a working state.

This continues #52 by @stsdc, rebased onto `v7.2` and fixed up until the
microphone actually records. His commit is kept as-is, with authorship intact;
everything else is on top.

## What was missing

Four separate problems, three of which turned out to be the same mistake.

| Fix | Effect without it |
|---|---|
| `pinctrl`: `swr_tx_data` on LPI GPIO1 needs mux value 3, not 1 | data line never reaches the bus, `SWR bus clsh detected` on every boot, TX device stays `UNATTACHED` |
| `swr2`: add the wakeup interrupt (`GIC_SPI 500`) | TX device never leaves runtime suspend, sixteen `IRQ sync failed to resume`, ADSP audio service restarts and the card fails with `-EBUSY` — taking the speaker down too |
| `qcom,tx-port-mapping` `<2 3 4 5>` → `<2 2 3 4>`, 10 → 12 channels | ADCs land on the wrong ports, transport never programmed, capture reads silence |
| capture link uses `<&swr2 1>`, not `<&swr2 0>` | `sdw_stream_add_master()` never called, master `DPn_PORT_CTRL` stays zero, controller raises `RD_FIFO_UNDERFLOW` |

One more thing found on the way: the RX and VA macro nodes carried no `status`
property, so they were enabled on *every* sm7150 board - including ones with no
audio codec described at all, such as `sm7150-google-sunfish`. They are now
disabled by default like the TX macro and both controllers next to them, and
davinci turns them on as it already did.

Plus the parts #52 did not have yet: the codec node itself, the capture and VA
dai-links, `audio-routing`, and a `MultiMedia2` frontend.

### The common thread

The TX SoundWire controller on sm7150 has `qcom,dout-ports = <1>`, while the
reference board everything was copied from — `qcm6490-idp` — has none. That
single difference shifts **two** numbering schemes by one:

* master **ports**: the microphone inputs start at port 2, not port 1 (which is
  also why the `qcom,ports-*` arrays of `swr2` begin with `0xff`);
* controller **DAIs**: `qcom_swrm_register_dais()` makes the first
  `num_dout_ports` DAIs playback-only, so DAI 0 here is playback and is never
  given `hw_params` in a capture link.

`qcm6490-idp` can legitimately use `<1 1 2 3>` and `<&swr1 0>`; this board
cannot.

### Why capture needs its own frontend

With only `MultiMedia1`, playback and capture share one PCM, and capture cannot
set hw params while playback is running:

```
$ aplay -D hw:0,0 tone.wav &
$ arecord -D hw:0,0 -f S16_LE -r 48000 -c 1 -d 1 /dev/null
arecord: set_params:1462: Unable to install hw params:
```

So userspace can never hold a source and a sink at the same time — PulseAudio
gives up on the card entirely and falls back to `auto_null`. Adding
`MultiMedia2` for capture follows what other boards do (RB5 plays on
`MultiMedia2`, captures on `MultiMedia3`).

## Scope

Everything here is inert for the other sm7150 boards:

* `sm7150.dtsi` - all the added nodes are `status = "disabled"`, and the wakeup
  interrupt is on a disabled controller. Verified by building
  `sm7150-google-sunfish.dtb`: every macro and both SoundWire controllers come
  out disabled. Only `sm7150-xiaomi-davinci.dtsi` enables them.
* `pinctrl-sm7150-lpass-lpi.c` - `swr_tx_data` only moves from mux slot 1 to
  slot 3 on GPIO1; nothing is removed, GPIO2 and GPIO5 are untouched. The
  function is requested through `tx_swr_active`, referenced solely by the TX
  macro, which is disabled unless a board enables it. The other boards touch
  `&lpass_tlmm` only for `gpio-line-names` and `gpio-reserved-ranges`.
* `sm7150-xiaomi-davinci.dtsi` - this board only.

Tested on the Samsung panel variant; the Visionox one shares the same dtsi and
differs only in the display.

## Testing

Xiaomi Mi 9T (SM7150-AA, Samsung panel), postmarketOS, kernel `v7.2`.

Both SoundWire buses attach with no clashes, the card comes up on every boot,
and the built-in microphone records:

```
noise floor            -62 dBFS
signal to noise ratio   62 dB   (1 kHz acoustic tone)
frequency accuracy      200/400/800/1600/3200/6400 Hz reproduced within
                        measurement error - no sample rate drift
linearity               x1.99, x1.95, x1.94 for successive input doublings
```

Speech recordings are clean. Speaker playback is unaffected.

The microphone sits on `AMIC1` -> codec `ADC1` -> master port 2, which matches
the vendor routing (`"TX SWR_ADC0", "ADC1_OUTPUT"`).

## Userspace note

`ADC2` and `ADC3` must be left off: they share master port 2 with `ADC1`, and
enabling them halves the signal and mixes the neighbouring channel into the
capture stream (noise floor goes from -62 to -20 dBFS). A UCM profile for this
board should disable them explicitly — that part belongs to `alsa-ucm-conf`, not
here.

## Not included

The earpiece is still missing, and the card does not survive an ADSP restart —
`wcd937x_soc_codec_probe()` fails with `-EBUSY` on the second probe. Both are
existing issues, unrelated to this series.

title: media: qcom: camss: sm7150: raise the interconnect bandwidth request
head: 3145bda86f477beaf5c31833215ddc1b2c7dada0
body:
## media: qcom: camss: sm7150: raise the interconnect bandwidth request

### Problem

On the Xiaomi Mi 9T (`xiaomi,davinci`) the front sensor, S5K3T2 at 2592x1940 raw10
30 fps, dies within a few seconds of streaming whenever the CPU is also working the
memory — which on this device means any time libcamera's software debayer is running.

The visible failure is a stalled pipeline: userspace stops getting buffers and the
camera application hangs. The kernel log shows CSI-2 lane FIFO overflow on the
receiver (`CSID_CSI2_RX_IRQ_STATUS = 0x01dbc0ff`: lane 0/1/2 overflow, CRC and ECC
errors, incomplete frame), followed by IOMMU context faults from the write master.

The faults are a symptom. Measured during a stall: the pipeline was hung for 31
seconds without a single new fault, while faults appeared before and after the
window. The receiver dies first; the write master runs on afterwards.

### Root cause

`icc_res_sm7150` asks the fabric for 2 GiB/s, applied once in `camss_runtime_resume()`
and dropped on power down. Sampling during a live stall confirms the request never
changes and the CAMNOC clock stays where `vfe_set_clock_rates()` puts it.

### Measurements

One run of that sensor per step, on the device, nothing else changed:

| interconnect request | CAMNOC clock | result |
|---|---|---|
| 2 GiB/s (current) | 150 MHz | stalls within seconds |
| 3 GiB/s | 150 MHz | stalls within seconds |
| **4 GiB/s** | 150 MHz | **runs clean, 0 IOMMU faults** |
| 6 GiB/s | 150 MHz | runs clean, 0 IOMMU faults |
| 2 GiB/s | 320 MHz | stalls within seconds |
| 6 GiB/s | 320 MHz | runs clean, 0 IOMMU faults |

The last two rows separate the two resources: raising the CAMNOC clock with the old
request changes nothing, raising the request with the stock clock fixes it. This patch
therefore touches only the request; `vfe_set_clock_rates()` is left alone.

After the change, with no module parameters and nothing else tuned: 15 camera sessions,
0 context faults, 0 VFE/CSID errors.

### Why the number is not derived from the stream

The sensor writes about 190 MB/s (2592 × 1940 × 10 bits × 30 fps). The request that
keeps it alive is twenty times that. So this is not paying for the camera's own
traffic — it asks the fabric and the DDR behind it to run at an operating point where
a busy memory bus still leaves the receiver served.

Worth stating explicitly, because the obvious "improvement" would make things worse: a
bandwidth model computed from resolution × frame rate × bits would request ~0.2 GB/s,
below even the current value.

### Note on the constant being replaced

`2097152` is not a measured figure for sm7150 — the identical constant appears for
2290, sm6150, sm6350, sm8250 and the other platforms in this file. Mainline
`icc_res_sm6150` carries the same value; whether that platform has the same problem is
untested here, and this patch does not touch it.

### What was tested

- Device: Xiaomi Mi 9T (`xiaomi,davinci`), postmarketOS, kernel `7.1.0-sm7150` from
  this branch at `fd78d17954a8`.
- Sensors exercised: front S5K3T2 through `csiphy1 → csid0 → vfe0_rdi0`, rear OV8856
  through `csiphy3`.
- Both libcamera (Plasma Camera) and raw V4L2 via `media-ctl` + `v4l2-ctl`.

### Known limitations

- All four interconnect paths are scaled together, because the experiment scaled them
  together. Which single path carries the fix, and whether `avg` or `peak` is the one
  that matters, is not separated.
- One run per step of the ladder; no long soak and no cold-boot series yet.
- Only davinci was available. Other sm7150 devices are untested.

Happy to run further measurements on request — the device is on the bench.

title: arm64: dts: qcom: sunfish: enable PM6150 fuel gauge + charging
head: c9bdf8500b8f49a8c6876d8f4c7a2ee43d62db1a
body:
Enables the PM6150 fuel gauge and SMB2 charger on sunfish. Added a simple-battery node with the downstream 3080mAh ATL/LSN pack data and wired the charger into the gauge and the Type-C connector so TCPM actually draws power. Also makes qcom_qg report charging/discharging status instead of always UNKNOWN, using power_supply_am_i_supplied().

Tested on two 4a units running mainline from this tree, mine and @truongsinh's independently. Capacity/voltage/current/temp all show up under /sys/class/power_supply/qcom_qg and charging status tracks the cable correctly.
